Requirement: The system shall maintain a single approved Chart of Accounts of 145 accounts as migrated from the authoritative workbook, with bilingual names, type, parent, level, posting flag and active flag.
The system shall prevent posting to non-posting parent accounts and to inactive accounts.
Every change to the Chart of Accounts shall require approval and be written to the audit log with previous and new values.

The system shall maintain analytical dimensions separately from accounts: project, cost centre, responsibility centre, counterparty, funding source, funding batch, funding category, contract, work package, CAPEX/OPEX, asset class and handover requirement.
Database entity(ies): projects, cost_centers, responsibility_centers, counterparties, funding_*, contracts, work_packages

Requirement: Contractors and suppliers shall be maintained as counterparties in a subsidiary ledger and shall never be created as cost centres.
The system shall record one journal header per transaction with any number of debit and credit lines.
The system shall reject any transaction whose total debit does not equal its total credit.
A journal line shall carry either a debit or a credit, never both and never zero.
The user interface shall offer a simplified two-account entry screen for ordinary transactions while storing them in the normalised header and line structure.
Project and cost centre shall be mandatory on every journal line.
The system shall implement the thirty-nine approved transaction types with declarative posting rules held in configuration rather than in code.
The system shall enforce the workflow Draft → Submitted → Reviewed → Approved → Posted, with maker–checker separation.
A posted entry shall not be editable or deletable; correction shall occur only through controlled reversal or adjustment.
The journal number shall be system-generated, unique and gapless within its sequence.
Shareholder funding shall never be recognised as revenue, and the spending of project funds shall never reduce a shareholder loan.
The system shall distinguish the funding source, the legal accounting owner of the funding, the actual payment source, cash received by SHH and direct payment on behalf of SHH.
The system shall distinguish capital contribution, shareholder loan, shareholder current account, repayment and conversion to equity.
Funding from a non-shareholder shall be recognised as a payable to that party and never as a shareholder loan.
The system shall maintain a shareholder funding subsidiary ledger reconciled to the general ledger control accounts.
The system shall trace funding through the chain shareholder → cash → advance or direct payment → final economic account and report the difference at each level.
Issuing an advance shall never be recognised as an expense; cost is recognised only when the advance is settled on approved documents.
When an advance is settled, the advance account shall be credited and no expense, CIP, fixed-asset or receivable account shall ever be credited to settle it.
The advance record shall carry holder, project, responsibility centre, purpose, amount, issue date, settlement deadline, amount settled, amount outstanding, supporting documents and status.
The system shall report advance aging against the settlement deadline and raise an exception when an advance becomes overdue.
Unsupported custody spend shall be reclassifiable to a personal receivable of the named individual under approval.

The contractor and supplier subledger shall report contract value, amendments, change orders, certified work, invoices, advances, advance recoveries, retention, deductions, taxes, penalties, payments, accrued amounts, outstanding payable and remaining commitment.
The contractor subledger shall reconcile to the related general ledger control accounts and the difference shall be reported.
Cumulative advance recovery shall not exceed the advance issued, and payment shall not exceed the outstanding payable.
The system shall maintain a Concession Assets under Construction register per account and per project with opening, additions, transfers out and closing, and an asset handover classification.

Transfer from CIP to the concession and operating right, and any amortization, shall be blocked until the commercial operation date parameter is set by an authorised user. The system shall never infer that date.
Revenue shall be recognised only in accounts 410001–410009 and every revenue line shall carry a government-share eligibility flag.
The government revenue share shall be computed on eligible revenue only, using an effective-dated parameter, and shall never be hardcoded.
The government share shall be recognised as a liability and presented as a profit and loss line, with a reconciliation of share due, share recognised, payments and closing payable.

The trial balance shall be fully system-generated with account code, bilingual names, opening debit and credit, period debit and credit, closing debit and credit, and shall prove total debit equals total credit on every run.
No manual balancing adjustment shall ever be used to force the trial balance to balance.

Every financial statement figure shall derive from the general ledger through a configurable mapping of account to statement line, sign and display order. No report figure shall be stored, typed or overridden.
The system shall produce a Statement of Financial Position with the approved groupings and a balance check of assets less liabilities and equity equal to zero.

The system shall produce a Profit and Loss statement showing gross project revenue, government revenue share, net retained revenue, direct operating costs, gross operating result, administrative expenses and net result.
The system shall produce a statutory cash flow statement and, separately named, a management funding and cash movement summary. The two shall not be presented as the same report.
The system shall produce a Statement of Changes in Equity.
Financial reporting shall support current month, prior month, current year to date, prior-year year to date, project-specific, corporate, consolidated, variance and percentage-change presentations.
The Cash Position shall derive every book balance from posted transactions and shall never operate as an independent ledger.

The Cash Position shall record opening balance, receipts, payments, closing book balance, actual balance, reconciled balance, variance, reconciliation status, last reconciliation date, responsible accountant and supporting documentation, with drill-down to the underlying entries.
Every report figure shall support drill-down from financial statement to trial balance to account ledger to journal entry to supporting document.

The system shall provide a consistent filter engine across reports covering dates, year, period, entity, project, cost centre, responsibility centre, account, account group, funding dimensions, counterparties, contract, work package, CAPEX/OPEX and status fields.
The system shall support formal accounting periods with open, soft close, final close, reopen with authorisation and lock, and shall reject postings into a closed or locked period.
The system shall operate a twenty-five task monthly closing checklist and shall block the final close of a period whose tasks are incomplete.
Journal entries shall support attached evidence with a controlled document status of Complete, Partial or Missing.
Missing and partial documents shall remain visible in the exceptions and compliance reporting and shall not be removable.
The system shall detect duplicate transactions and duplicate document references and require a disposition before posting.
The system shall maintain an exceptions register in which every unresolved item remains visible at its true value; no exception shall be deleted, netted or forced into an account.
Any posting to the suspense account shall automatically open an exception, and clearing it shall require a resolution reference.
Historical entries whose source carries no date shall be recorded with an explicit date status and a null transaction date; the system shall never substitute a date.

The system shall record a complete audit trail of creation, modification, submission, review, approval, posting, reversal, period locks, master data changes, mapping changes and reconciliation balances, with user, timestamp, reason, previous value and new value.
The system shall implement role-based access control across the eight defined roles and the seventeen defined permissions, with no single user holding uncontrolled end-to-end authority.
The system shall migrate the historical accounting data from the approved source workbook without altering dates, amounts, descriptions, classifications or exceptions.

Migrated data shall reconcile to the source workbook on record count, total debit, total credit, per-account balances, project totals, funding totals, advance balances, duplicate counts and exceptions before the system is accepted.
The user interface shall support Arabic with correct right-to-left rendering, bilingual labels and IQD formatting without decimals.
Financial tables shall support search, filter, sort, drill-down, export to Excel, export to PDF, print, date filters and saved views.
The executive dashboard shall present live accounting data with a management purpose and drill-down behind every indicator.

The system shall hold policy parameters — government share percentage, contract term, commercial operation date, FX rate, currency and decimal policy — in an effective-dated parameter table with approval and full history.

The system shall meet the non-functional requirements for authentication, authorisation, audit logging, data integrity, backup and restore, performance, attachment storage, encryption, session security, disaster recovery, export, scalability, Arabic support and browser compatibility.
